summary: The rewrite's target can be reached, and the rules allow it, including PDL weight prefetch before griddepcontrol.wait and the hi+lo router at T=1. But the stage-1 gain is overstated: at T=1 the pooler already streams at about 3.2 TB/s and the router is hidden on the side stream, so most of the saving must come from removing nodes, which LESSONS records as weak. The 288-CTA x 128 KB grid runs in 2.2 waves at 1 CTA/SM, and that is the biggest risk to M2.
justification: Mechanism: at T<=32 the dense pre-expert chain is a serial run of bandwidth- and latency-bound launches, and decode_1 sits at 145.6 us against a 40 us floor. Collapsing pooler + splitKreduce + router + routing + mod + expert_map gather + contiguous + cast + align + F.rms_norm into 2 kernels is plausible on H200, and the profile rows confirm the replaced kernels exist and cost something. At decode_1: vectorized_layer_norm (F.rms_norm) is 5.9 us, splitKreduce 5.0 us over 3 calls, the fp32 dot_kernel router 5.0 us, _moe_align_small_numel 3.6 us at verify_1, and vectorized_elementwise 2.8 us over 3 calls. The expected directions match TASK.md: T<=32 shapes faster, and verify_16/32 (T=128/256) flat because they are outside the config gate, which is a good built-in control. Corrections to the arithmetic: (1) The decode_1 row nvjet_sm90_tst_128x8_64x12_4x1_v_bz_splitK_TNT, 32.6 us, is 2 calls (qkv 37.7 MB + pooler 67.1 MB = 105 MB, about 3.2 TB/s), not the pooler alone. The pooler is about 21 us plus its share of splitKreduce. P moving 75.5 MB at 3.8 TB/s is 19.9 us, so the stream-bandwidth gain at T=1 is only about 2-4 us. (2) The router (8.4 MB) today runs concurrently on the side stream. Folding it into P puts its bytes on the critical path, so the side-stream removal is mostly a node-count win, not a byte win. (3) Removing small nodes was measured neutral twice on this exact chain (expert-id-map-single-kernel 1.037x, moe-align-single-kernel-small-t 1.043x, both within CI). The realistic stage-1 saving is about 8-14 us on decode_1 and verify_1 and about 6-12 us at T=16/32: +5-9% on those shapes and about +2-4% headline, not +4-6%. A 2-4% headline gain is still readable from per-shape rows and replaced-kernel time, which is how a rewrite is judged. Weakest link: the P design's own bandwidth. 4608 rows / 32 = 144 row tiles x SPLIT_K 2 = 288 CTAs. Each holds 128 KB of smem, so only 1 CTA/SM fits (228 KB/SM), and the grid runs in waves of 132/132/24: the last wave streams with 18% of the SMs, and two wave ramps are exposed. M2 (<=20 us at T=1) is unlikely as written. Fix before building: either (a) a persistent or stream-K grid of 132 CTAs walking (row tile, k-chunk) units, or (b) a 64-96 KB ring (e.g. 4 stages x 32 rows x 256 k = 64 KB) so 2-3 CTAs/SM keep all 288 resident in one wave. Little's law needs only about 5-8 MB in flight chip-wide at 4.8 TB/s (264 x 64 KB = 17 MB is plenty); the 3.73 TB/s LESSONS figure came from a Triton grid shaped differently. A second measurement caveat: the profiler charges a PDL-launched kernel's row with its wait on the predecessor ('an overlapping kernel's time includes any wait for the one before it'), so P's top_kernels row will read high when pdl=1. Time P in prepare() with CUDA events, with and without PDL, and print both, so M1/M2 are judged on P's stream time.
confounders: No landed hypotheses are listed for master, so no landed patch confounds this run. Master's in-file history does touch this region: sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8 (ROUTER_FP32_MAX_TOKENS=1, router_dtype=None at T>=2), marlin-block-m-cap-16 and post-expert-norm-triton-small-t (SMALL_T_POST_NORM=32). R must reproduce their contracts exactly: local_ids -1 for remote slots (the _post_norm_combine_kernel skips on eid<0 and never loads those y rows), topk_weights fp32 contiguous, and block_size_m from BLOCK_SIZE_M_CANDIDATES then capped at 16 (8 at T=1/8, 16 at T=16/32). Moving T=1 to hi+lo also means attn_boundary at T=1 must be asked for router_dtype=None (the fp32 router_input write goes away), which is a small extra saving, not a confounder.

In-flight bf16-shape-gated-triton-gemms-small-t (running, pooler at m<=16) and queued moe-align-small-t-restack-on-master replace the same rows. If either lands before this is claimed, the incumbent rows change (Triton pooler instead of nvjet+splitKreduce; one align launch). Judge M1 against whatever master is at claim time, not against the numbers quoted in the hypothesis.
interference: No companion is warranted. Nothing has landed on master's lineage that this change could interact with. The T>32 shapes are byte-identical and serve as an in-run drift control. The attribution question that matters (how much is P's stream, how much is node removal, how much is PDL) is answered more cheaply inside the run than with a second check: (1) the profile rows show P and R time against the vanished rows; (2) prepare() can time P with PDL on and off using CUDA events on synthetic input and print both, alongside the existing [small-t-dense-chain] line. A pdl=0 control run would only help if the prepare-time numbers are inconclusive, and then it is a cheap follow-up (flip the PDL launch attribute only). The brief also asks for a rewrite's follow-up to be its next stage, not a companion.
rules_flags: PDL is allowed. The rules forbid host syncs, value-dependent allocation or branching, caching anything derived from data, lower precision, and work outside the timed call; PDL breaks none of these. The pre-wait prefetch reads only prepare-time weights, inside the captured graph, after the judge's L2 flush, so it is neither input-derived caching nor out-of-call work. Make sure no input or predecessor-written buffer (ffn_input, local_start, the ticket buffer) is touched before griddepcontrol.wait, and that P writes no output before the wait.

PDL in CUDA graph capture: launching with cudaLaunchKernelEx and cudaLaunchAttributeProgrammaticStreamSerialization on a capturing stream records a programmatic dependency edge (CUDA 12.3+ runtime and driver). FA3 in sgl_kernel and SGLang/TRT-LLM kernels already use this under graphs on Hopper, so it can survive the judge's capture. Caveats: (a) the edge forms only when the immediately preceding captured node on that stream is a kernel node. If the predecessor is an event wait, memset or copy, capture can silently fall back to a full dependency, so 'capture succeeded' does not prove overlap. The self-check should confirm the edge type (cudaGraphGetEdges with edge data, or the prepare-time timing). (b) The predecessor (SGLang's JIT FusedPostNormResidualPreNorm) never calls griddepcontrol.launch_dependents, so P can launch only once every primary CTA has exited, and the overlap is about 1-2 us of launch latency and memory flush. The hypothesis acknowledges this. (c) The fallback path (capture error -> pdl=0) must be decided in prepare, never in kernel_fn.

The router hi+lo bf16 at T=1 is explicitly allowed ('at any batch size'). Interleaving hi and lo rows into W_pr is a lossless repack. Rounding the router's activation to bf16 at T=1 (reading ffn_input instead of the fp32 router_input) matches what SGLang and master already do at T>=2, which the rules cite.
The ticket and semaphore buffers held in state are scratch, not values derived from data. They must be reset in-kernel on every call (atomic_xchg by the winner) so graph replays stay correct.
load_inline invokes nvcc, which the technical rules explicitly sanction. Keep the compile inside the 15-minute budget, including the prepare self-check across 6 T values and one graph capture.
Precision: expert_input stays bf16, the RMSNorm runs fp32 math with bf16 output (matching F.rms_norm on a bf16 input), logits are fp32 and topk_weights fp32. All OK.
open_questions: Which grid will P actually use: 288 x 128 KB at 1 CTA/SM (2.2 waves), a persistent/stream-K 132-CTA grid, or a smaller ring at 2-3 CTAs/SM? Pick before building; M2 depends on it.

Does the PDL edge actually form in the captured graph? Is P's predecessor at T<=32 a kernel node on the main stream once the side-stream fork/join is gone? Check the edge type in the prepare self-check, not just capture success.
Does the profile row for P include its PDL wait? Print prepare-time CUDA-event timings of P with pdl=0 and pdl=1 so M1/M2 are judged on the kernel's own stream time.

R's last-program align must match moe_align_block_size's sentinel, padding and -1 handling exactly at block_size_m 8 and 16, and the buffer sizes Marlin expects. Is comparing Marlin output y on synthetic skewed routing (including all-remote tokens and a single hot expert) enough coverage? Add a T where no slot is local.

Tie-break order in top-8 must match FusedMuseSparkRouting, or at least stay inside the judge's 0.05/0.03 routing tolerances. Equality is checked only on tie-free data; one near-tie synthetic case would give confidence.

If bf16-shape-gated-triton-gemms-small-t lands first, does this still beat the Triton pooler row it installs (likely about 3.7 TB/s)? If not, stage 1's win is mostly node removal, and the headline expectation should be revised down.
